::: {.mkt-hero}
<span class="mkt-eyebrow">Markdown in · live HTML out</span>

<h1>Technical writing at the<br><span class="mkt-accent">speed of code</span></h1>

<p class="mkt-lead">A focused dev server that turns one&nbsp;<code>.qmd</code> file into a live blog post, slide deck, book, or website. Save, and only the block you changed re-renders, in place. No cold start. No full-page reload.</p>

<span class="mkt-eyebrow">Why it feels different</span>
## Three things it gets right

The whole tool is built around one idea: writing should feel as immediate as editing code.
:::

::: {.feature-grid}
<div class="feature">
  <h3><span class="mkt-ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="13 2 3 14 12 14 11 22 21 10 12 10 13 2"></polygon></svg></span>Block-level updates</h3>
  <p>A save re-renders only the blocks that changed, and swaps them in place over a websocket. The page never reloads, so live Three.js and Observable canvases keep their state.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature">
  <h3><span class="mkt-ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3"></circle><path d="M12 2v3M12 19v3M2 12h3M19 12h3"></path></svg></span>Click to source</h3>
  <p>Every rendered block remembers the line it came from. Double-click anything in the preview to jump straight to its source — even across <code>{{< include >}}</code>d files.</p>
</div>
<div class="feature">
  <h3><span class="mkt-ico"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 2c1.5 3 4 4.5 4 8a4 4 0 0 1-8 0c0-1.2.4-2.2 1-3"></path><path d="M12 22a6 6 0 0 0 6-6c0-2-1-3.7-2.5-5"></path></svg></span>No cold start</h3>
  <p>A long-running server and a warm Jupyter kernel mean edits show up immediately, and a code change re-runs only that cell and everything downstream — not the whole document.</p>
</div>
:::
:::

::: {.mkt-section}

<span class="mkt-eyebrow">One source, many outputs</span>
## The same `.qmd` becomes any of these

Write once in plain text. Pick the output in the front matter. Every format shares the block model, the offline math and highlighting, and the live edit loop.
:::

<span class="mkt-eyebrow">The part you can't screenshot</span>
## Edit the code. The output re-runs in place.

A `{python}` or `{r}` cell runs against a warm kernel. Change a parameter and only that cell — and the figure it produced — re-renders. The rest of the page never moves.
:::

::: {.mkt-media}
<figure>
  <div class="mkt-media-frame">
    <video src="assets/live-code.mp4" autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
  </div>
  <figcaption>One value changes in the source; the matplotlib figure updates in place, with scroll preserved. Double-click any block to open its source in your editor.</figcaption>
</figure>
:::
:::

<p class="mkt-dogfood">There is nothing static here that a screenshot could fake: <strong>this landing page, its <a href="docs/">documentation book</a>, and the slide deck above are all built and served by qmd-fast</strong> — from plain <code>.qmd</code> files in one repository.</p>

Author in `.qmd`, preview it live, and ship self-contained HTML — a post, a deck, a book, or a site.
